newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slightly firmer at start of bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares slightly firmer at start of bourse.

text.p: German shares were slightly firmer in early bourse dealings on Friday, seeking to keep up their advance on new record levels ahead of the weekend despite overnight Wall Street losses.
The 30-share DAX index was up 5.97 points at 3,811.26 points, while the IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was down 7.55 points at 3,812.61 points.
"Dealings are relatively quiet this morning but there's no sign that the market is going to break down anytime soon," said one Frankfurt trader. "The uptrend appears to still be intact."
A lack of fresh corporate news kept dealings focused on technical market factors, which traders said pointed to gains.
They specifically said the market was keen on automobile shares as Volkswagen AG was among the top gainers, rising 38 marks to 1,315 marks.
Luxury carmaker BMW AG was also higher on the day, rising four marks to 1,431 marks, while Daimler-Benz AG, maker of Mercedes vehicles, was down 20 pfennigs at 141.80 marks.
"A lot of the banks are telling clients to take another look at the carmakers, that they have not kept up the other sectors in this rally," said one trader.

Among other shares, airline Lufthansa AG was down 80 pfennigs at 34.20 marks despite saying on Thursday at its annual general meeting that it expected first-half profit to be higher than in the 1995 and 1996 periods.
Traders said the drop in Lufthansa was due mainly to profit-taking after a recent sharp advance in the share.
